newsitem.title: USA: Analysts see US winter wheat crop at 1.579 bln bu.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see US winter wheat crop at 1.579 bln bu.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department will likely increase its forecast for U.S. winter wheat production in Thursday's crop production report, grain analysts said.

"I think crop conditions came up," said Joel Karlin, analyst with Everen Securities. "The temperatures were almost ideal when the crop was filling grain, especially in frost-affected areas. We also saw timely precipitation."
USDA will release its June winter wheat production estimates on Thursday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
A Reuter survey of analysts produced an average trade estimate of 1.579 billion bushels for all winter wheat. USDA in May put output at roughly 1.561 billion bushels.

Several analysts noted weather patterns were more conducive for crop development in May than they were in April. Wheat futures at all three exchanges rallied in April after a late-season cold snap hit key hard red winter wheat regions of Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas.
But crop tours later showed damage was probably not as severe as many had thought.
Rich Feltes, vice-president and director of research for Refco Inc in Chicago, said winter wheat production would be roughly 25 million bushels larger than USDA's May forecast.
"Beneficial moisture, improving crop condition ratings and continued cooler-than-normal temperatures" boosted crop prospects since the May report, Feltes said.
"Wheat is a cool weather crop," he added. "The reason northern Europe has high yields is because of cool weather."
Hard red winter wheat harvest was just underway but yields from early-harvested fields in Texas were as good or better than expected, said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
"Early yields have been better than expected," Gidel said. He added that rain over Memorial Day weekend likely improved yield potential in Nebraska, northern Kansas, South Dakota and Montana.
The average analyst estimate for hard red winter wheat production was 899 million bushels, compared with USDA's May outlook for 894 million. Last year's production was pegged by USDA at 762 million.

The soft red winter wheat output estimate was also seen increasing slightly. Analysts pegged production at 413 million bushels, against USDA's May estimate of 409 million. Output in 1996 was 422 million bushels, according to USDA.
But Gidel cautioned that cool, wet weather late in the growing season can cause scab infestation and cut yields.

"I don't think USDA is going to change them a lot, but maybe they will edge them up on yields," Gidel said, referring to SRW numbers. "Scab can manifest itself in minutes, so I don't think USDA will want to raise that number and then turn around and lower it."
Analysts estimated white wheat production at 267 million bushels, up from USDA's May projection for 259 million but down from last year's output of 294 million bushels.
"White wheat production prospects look pretty solid out there and USDA was pretty conservative on its yield estimates," Everen's Karlin said.
